qs_073:n1.prompt:
You are helping me choose accounting software for my startup. Please research and compare accounting tools suitable for a small/early-stage company, treating the product I ultimately pick as {{vendor}} in your output (do not lock in a single real product as the final named answer — research actual well-known tools, but present the final recommendation section using {{vendor}} as the placeholder for whichever one best fits my needs).

If you don't already know it, ask me for: my monthly transaction volume, whether I need payroll/inventory/multi-currency support, my budget, whether I need integrations with a specific bank, payment processor, or invoicing tool, and my accounting basis (cash vs. accrual).

Actions to take:
1. Identify 3-5 candidate accounting tools appropriate for my stage and needs.
2. Compare them on: pricing tiers, ease of setting up a chart of accounts, bank feed/reconciliation support, invoicing and AR/AP features, reporting (P&L, balance sheet, cash flow), multi-user/permission support, integration ecosystem, and month-end close workflow support.
3. Note any free trial or free-tier availability.
4. Produce a scored comparison table and a short written recommendation naming {{vendor}} as the top pick with rationale tied to my stated needs.
5. Flag any tool that lacks accountant/bookkeeper collaboration features or CPA-firm compatibility, since that matters for month-end close.

Done looks like: a comparison table plus a clear recommendation paragraph identifying {{vendor}} and explaining tradeoffs versus the runner-up options.

Report back with the table, the recommendation, and a short list of open questions (if any) I should resolve before committing, such as confirming pricing tier or integration requirements.

qs_073:n2.prompt:
You are helping me set up accounting software for my company. If you don't already have it, ask me for: (1) my company's legal name, entity type, and industry; (2) my chosen accounting software, referred to below as {{vendor}}; (3) my email address to use for signup; and (4) any existing chart-of-accounts structure or preferences I want reflected (e.g., specific classes/tags for departments, locations, or projects).

Once you have this information:
1. Go to {{vendor}}'s signup page and create an account using my configured credentials, entering my company details as provided.
2. Complete any initial company-profile setup steps (industry, fiscal year start, currency) using the info I gave you.
3. Navigate to the chart of accounts setup area and configure it: create standard top-level account types (Assets, Liabilities, Equity, Income, Expenses), add sub-accounts appropriate to my industry (e.g., separate expense categories, bank accounts, revenue streams), and set up class or tag dimensions if I requested department/location/project tracking.
4. If {{vendor}} offers a default chart-of-accounts template for my industry, apply it as a starting point, then adjust/add accounts per my preferences.
5. Since this is an async signup flow, note that email verification or account activation may take time — check back and verify the account is fully active and the chart of accounts is saved before considering this done.

Done looks like: a verified, active {{vendor}} account with a saved chart of accounts containing the standard account types, relevant sub-accounts, and any requested class/tag dimensions, ready for monthly bookkeeping.

Report back with: the account status (verified/pending), a summary list of the account types and sub-accounts created, any class/tag dimensions configured, and any setup step you couldn't complete or that requires my input.

qs_073:n3.prompt:
You are helping me connect my business bank and credit-card feeds to {{vendor}}, the accounting software I've chosen, so transactions import automatically every day and my books can close monthly.

Before starting, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available:
- The list of bank accounts and credit cards used for business activity (bank name, account type, last 4 digits if known)
- Confirmation that I have configured credentials for {{vendor}} ready to use
- Whether I also want payments and payroll systems connected so their activity flows into the ledger

Then do the following:
1. Log into {{vendor}} using my configured credentials.
2. Navigate to the bank/card feed connection area (sometimes called "Banking" or "Bank Feeds").
3. For each account I listed, initiate the connection to the corresponding financial institution through {{vendor}}'s supported bank-linking flow, following any identity or account-selection prompts the bank presents.
4. Confirm each account shows a "connected" or "syncing" status and that recent transactions have started importing.
5. If I asked for payments or payroll systems to be connected, locate the relevant integration or app-connection settings in {{vendor}} and link those systems the same way, confirming they show as active.
6. Set the transaction import frequency to automatic/daily if {{vendor}} offers that option.
7. Note any account that fails to connect (e.g., requires manual verification, micro-deposits, or additional MFA the bank enforces) — that verification step remains a human step and I will complete it separately.

Done looks like: every bank and card account I specified is connected and actively importing transactions into {{vendor}}, any requested payments/payroll integrations are active, and import frequency is set to automatic.

Report back with: a list of accounts/systems successfully connected and syncing, any accounts still pending manual verification (and what's needed), and the import frequency setting confirmed.
